summary: Nir, CEO of TraceLoop, introduces OpenLLMetry, an open-source project that extends OpenTelemetry to support GenAI observability. He begins by explaining OpenTelemetry, a CNCF project (one of the largest after Kubernetes) that standardizes cloud observability across every major platform including Datadog, Dynatrace, New Relic, Grafana, and Honeycomb. OpenTelemetry is a protocol defining three data types: logging (arbitrary events emitted during application lifetime), metrics (aggregate-level measurements like CPU, memory, latency, or for GenAI, token usage and error rate), and traces (tracking multi-step processes across microservices, particularly relevant for GenAI chains, workflows, and agents). Beyond the protocol, OpenTelemetry is an ecosystem comprising SDKs (manual data emission in 11 languages), instrumentations (automatic data emission via monkey-patching client libraries with negligible latency impact), and collectors (self-deployable preprocessing components for filtering, obscuring PII, or routing to multiple providers). OpenLLMetry extends this ecosystem specifically for GenAI, providing 40+ instrumentations for foundation models (OpenAI, Anthropic, Cohere, Gemini, Bedrock), vector databases (Pinecone, Chroma), and frameworks (LangChain, LlamaIndex, CrewAI, Haystack). A Pinecone instrumentation example shows how queries, indexing, vector distances, scores, and latencies are captured in standard OpenTelemetry format. Because OpenLLMetry relies on the standard OpenTelemetry protocol, users are never tied to a specific observability platform and can switch between them via configuration changes.
